name: Scrape Portfolio Pages & Extract Project Credits with AI (Google Sheets)

parameters.content:
## Scrape Portfolio Pages & Extract Project Credits with AI (Google Sheets)

### How it works

1. Trigger the workflow manually to start processing.
2. Read page URLs from a Google Sheet, skipping any row already marked Done.
3. Fetch each page with browser-like headers, then clean and convert the HTML to text.
4. Use an AI agent to extract project credits from the text, logging failures as rows.
5. Append results and errors to the output sheet and mark the row processed.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Create one spreadsheet with two tabs.
- [ ] Input tab columns: Company | Website | Page URL | Status. Leave Status blank to start.
- [ ] Output tab columns: Company | Website | Page URL | Agency | Brand | Project Name | Full Page Content | Error.
- [ ] Connect Google Sheets credentials and pick your document and tab on all five Sheets nodes.
- [ ] Add an LLM credential to the Chat Model node. OpenAI by default; Anthropic, Gemini and Ollama drop in unchanged.

### Customization

The system message on Project Credit Extractor holds all the domain knowledge. Rewrite it, along with the parser's JSON example and the output column mappings, and the same skeleton handles any page-to-structured-rows job. Other knobs: the 15s timeout and User-Agent on Fetch Page Content, the 8000-character truncation in Transform HTML to Text, and the politeness delay in Wait 2 Seconds.

## Initialize workflow

Trigger manually to start execution.

## Fetch URLs from sheet

Get URLs from Google Sheets to process.

## Prepare and fetch HTML

Prepare requests and fetch HTML content.

## Handle fetch results

Check HTML fetch success and clean data for AI.

## Extract credits with AI

Use AI to extract project credits from clean text.

## Record results and errors

Append extracted data and errors to Google Sheets.

options.systemMessage:
=You extract structured project credits from a supplier's portfolio or case-study page.

CONTEXT
Company: {{ $json.company }}
Page URL: {{ $json.url }}

WHAT YOU ARE LOOKING AT
This page belongs to a supplier — an agency, studio, production house, consultancy,
fabricator, or freelancer — showing work they delivered for other people. Your job is to
identify, for each distinct project on the page, who commissioned the work and who it was
ultimately for.

FIELDS TO EXTRACT

1. AGENCY — the commissioning intermediary
The entity that hired {{ $json.company }} to do this work, when that entity is itself a
middleman rather than the end customer.
Look for labels: "Agency", "Commissioned by", "Produced for", "In collaboration with",
"Client", "For", "With".
Names often contain: Agency, Creative, Studio, Production, Media, Digital, Group, Partners.
Large agency networks worth recognising: BBDO, TBWA, Ogilvy, VML, McCann, FCB, Havas,
Wieden+Kennedy, DDB, Grey, Leo Burnett, Saatchi & Saatchi, Publicis, Dentsu.

Do NOT put in this field:
- {{ $json.company }} itself — the page owner is never their own agency
- A recognisable consumer brand, retailer, or broadcaster — that is the BRAND, not the agency
- A peer supplier. If the named entity's own positioning is "we make things for clients"
  in the same craft as {{ $json.company }}, it is a peer, not a commissioning agency
- Any individual person. Producer, director, and creative-director names are credits,
  not organisations. "Producer: Jane Doe" yields nothing for this field
- Generic labels. "Client", "Direct to Client", "Client Acme" — extract the real entity name
  or nothing

Set to null when: no intermediary is named, only the end brand appears, only the page
owner is credited, only individuals are listed, or you are choosing between brand and
agency and cannot tell. Null always beats a wrong guess.

2. BRAND — the end customer
The organisation whose product, service, or message the work promotes. Consumer brands,
tech companies, broadcasters, retailers, nonprofits, government bodies, universities.
Usually the most recognisable name in the credits and the entity that ultimately benefits.
If both a brand and an agency appear, the brand goes here and the agency goes above.
Extract the parent brand, not the product line — "Nike", not "Air Jordan".

3. PROJECT NAME — the campaign, film, or engagement title
Take it as written, even if it includes the company's own name. Cleaning happens downstream.

OUTPUT
Return a projects array. One object per distinct project visible on the page — index and
portfolio-listing pages will produce many. Skip entries with no usable information rather
than padding the array with nulls.

WORKED EXAMPLES

Credits read: "Client: Nike / Agency: Wieden+Kennedy Portland / Animation: {{ $json.company }}"
{"agency": "Wieden+Kennedy Portland", "brand": "Nike", "project_name": "Play New"}

Credits read: "For: Netflix / Directed by John Smith"  (no intermediary)
{"agency": null, "brand": "Netflix", "project_name": "Series Title Sequence"}

COMMON ERRORS
Brand duplicated into the agency field:
  WRONG {"agency": "Nike", "brand": "Nike"}   RIGHT {"agency": null, "brand": "Nike"}
A person promoted to an organisation:
  WRONG {"agency": "Jane Doe", "brand": "Adidas"}   RIGHT {"agency": null, "brand": "Adidas"}
A peer supplier mistaken for the commissioner:
  WRONG {"agency": "Another Production Studio", "brand": "Meta"}   RIGHT {"agency": null, "brand": "Meta"}
A label captured instead of a name:
  WRONG {"agency": "Client Acme", "brand": "Acme"}   RIGHT {"agency": null, "brand": "Acme"}

PRIORITISE
Commissioned commercial work: campaigns, advertising, product launches, branded content,
social and experiential.
DE-PRIORITISE
Self-initiated work, personal or art projects, and festival pieces with no commissioning party.
